books.section: Topic 3.13 Continuity and Change in Period 3

stimulus.text:
| | 1763 | 1800 |
|---|---|---|
| Ruler | A king in London, with royal governors in the colonies | An elected president and Congress under a written Constitution |
| National legislature | None elected by Americans; Parliament made the laws | Congress, with a House elected by voters and a Senate chosen by state legislatures |
| Voting | Limited to men with property in most colonies | Still limited to men with property in most states |

New Jersey's constitution of 1776 let “all inhabitants” worth £50 vote, so some women voted there. Laws in 1790 and 1797 made that plain. In 1807 the legislature limited the vote to white men.

stem: New Jersey let some women vote from 1776 until 1807, when the vote was limited to white men. What does the New Jersey case best show?

options.text: Women voted in every state after independence in 1776.
options.misconception: Background: no other state let women vote; New Jersey was the one exception.

options.text: Women voted for a time, then lost the vote in 1807.
New Jersey women kept the vote even after the 1807 law.
options.misconception: The 1807 law limited the vote to white men, so women lost it.

options.text: The 1807 law extended the vote to enslaved people as well.
options.misconception: The 1807 law narrowed the vote to white men; it extended it to no one.

rationales.A: Background: no other state let women vote; New Jersey was the one exception.
rationales.B: Revolutionary words opened voting to some New Jersey women for about thirty years, then the 1807 law closed it again.
rationales.C: The 1807 law limited the vote to white men, so women lost it.
rationales.D: The 1807 law narrowed the vote to white men; it extended it to no one.
rationales.general:
1. Read the note: New Jersey's 1776 constitution let “all inhabitants” worth £50 vote, and laws in 1790 and 1797 made clear that women could vote.
2. Some women did vote there for about thirty years.
3. In 1807 the legislature limited the vote to white men, and women lost it.
4. So revolutionary words opened a door for some women, then the law closed it again.
Remember: one exception tests a rule, so ask whether it lasted.
